question: Will Mitch McConnell speak this year?
resolution_criteria:
Will there be any video / audio recording / other evidence of Mitch McConnell speaking from today (July 7th) until the end of the year.  I must be able to view/hear it with my own eyes/ears.  If an extremely credible source (NYT? WaPo? idk) releases an article that corroborates Mitch McConnell speaking (say, a journalist spoke with him), that would count.  Using augmented voice technology to speak would count as well.

I will not bet on this market.
research:
I couldn't find any audio or video of Mitch McConnell speaking between July 7 and August 27, 2026. The best evidence for a "yes" is that people who talked with him by phone around July 7 said so publicly, but those are second-hand accounts. Most source pages wouldn't load for me, so the facts below come mostly from search-result summaries, and some dates are inferred.

### 1. Resolution source
- The question doesn't name a URL. It resolves on any video or audio of McConnell speaking, or a highly credible outlet confirming he spoke, between July 7 and December 31, 2026.
- The likely places for such evidence are his Senate press page, C-SPAN and major news outlets. His press page carries written statements dated July and August 2026 ([July statement](https://www.mcconnell.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2026/7/statement-from-senator-mitch-mcconnell), [August update](https://www.mcconnell.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2026/8/update-from-senator-mitch-mcconnell)), and I found no audio or video posted with them.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-07-07: Majority Leader John Thune's office said he spoke with McConnell on Monday, July 6, in a "lengthy and substantive conversation." Whip John Barrasso's spokesperson said Barrasso talked with him by phone for 20 minutes on Tuesday, which works out to July 7, and that McConnell "was fully engaged." Former adviser Scott Jennings said he had a nearly 20-minute call with him the same Tuesday. ([UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2026/07/07/senate-gop-leaders-say-they-have-talked-to-mcconnell/5831783457986/), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5957438-mcconnell-thune-barrasso-health/), [NOTUS](https://www.notus.org/senate/thune-republican-leaders-mitch-mcconnell-hospital))
  - If July 7 counts as inside the window, this may qualify. But these are claims by aides and allies that newspapers repeated, not a journalist speaking with him directly.
- 2026-07-07: The Daily Caller raised doubts about whether he was conscious when the earliest call supposedly took place. That was the outlet's framing, not an established fact. ([Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2026/07/07/emails-mcconnell-health-response/))
- I found no audio, video or direct interview by August 27. Nothing settles the question yet.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: Northeastern ran a piece headlined "Ten Weeks Later, Where's Senator Mitch McConnell?", describing him as still absent and out of public view. ([Northeastern](https://news.northeastern.edu/2026/08/19/sen-mitch-mcconnell-health-update/))
- About 2026-08-06/07: He said in a written statement that he had left the rehab center and would do intensive physical therapy at home during the August recess. He gave no date for returning to the Senate. ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/06/mitch-mcconnell-health-update-senate-gop.html), [NPR/WHQR](https://www.whqr.org/2026-08-07/sen-mitch-mcconnell-says-he-has-been-discharged-from-rehab-center-to-recover-at-home), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/6/us-senator-mcconnell-says-hes-been-discharged-from-rehab-center))
  - Newsweek says video of him leaving the facility shows him waving, smiling and giving a thumbs-up. No speech is reported. ([Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/how-mitch-mcconnell-new-appearance-compares-last-time-12442437))
- 2026-07-27: His office released a written update and a photo. It said he was doing "intense physical therapy" and had missed 38 votes since June 14. ([NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/mcconnell-releases-health-update-not-ready-return-work-rcna589452))
- Late July (date approximate): The Senate's attending physician said his childhood polio still significantly limits his mobility. ([Scripps](https://www.scrippsnews.com/politics/mcconnell-remains-in-rehab-not-yet-cleared-to-return-to-work))
- 2026-07-12: His first statement since being hospitalized was written, with a photo. He said he fell, was "briefly unconscious" and later had pneumonia, with no broken bones, concussion or stroke. ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/12/mcconnell-provides-health-update-after-long-unexplained-absence.html), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/12/politics/mitch-mcconnell-hospital-announcement))
- 2026-06-14: He was hospitalized after a fall.
- Pattern so far: everything has come as written statements and photos, and critics have noted he "has not released any video message."

### 4. Base rates
- In earlier health episodes, he came back and spoke publicly:
  - After a 2023 fall and concussion, he was out for about six weeks, then returned to the Senate floor and spoke on camera.
  - After his 2023 freezing episodes, he gave a public speech in Kentucky within weeks. ([Yahoo](https://news.yahoo.com/mitch-mcconnell-makes-first-public-201632323.html?fr=sycsrp_catchall))
- This episode is longer: more than ten weeks without public speech by August 19.
- He is 84 and retires in January 2027. As a sitting senator, he would almost certainly be seen and heard by reporters if he returns to the Capitol before then.

### 5. Other forecasts
- About August 2026: Polymarket's market on whether McConnell casts a Senate vote by August 31 was reported at roughly 1% "Yes." ([Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/mcconnell-public-appearance-prediction-market-odds-2026/))
- Kalshi's market on him resigning early reportedly fell from 29% to 17% after the July 12 statement. ([Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/mcconnell-public-appearance-prediction-market-odds-2026/))
- I couldn't find the Manifold market for this question or any other market specifically about him speaking.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early September 2026: The Senate comes back from August recess. If he returns to vote, reporters at the Capitol are very likely to hear him speak or record him.
- Fall 2026: Senate sessions run through the November 8 midterms and into the lame-duck period. Farewell speeches by retiring senators usually happen in November and December.
- Any time: He could release a video or audio message, or give an interview.
- Risks to a "yes":
  - His health could get worse.
  - He could resign early.
  - His staff could keep limiting him to written statements.
